newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks end firmer, optimism drives market.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks end firmer, optimism drives market.

text.p: Croatian stocks forged ahead on Thursday as top shares set new records in another bullish session on the Zagreb bourse.
Traders said the market was moved by a pervasive feeling of optimism which was not bound to end soon though growth may not continue as strongly as it has been in the past three weeks.
"You can feel the bullish mood strongly, but how long it will last is hard to tell. It might not keep up such a pace," said Marko Nikolac of Metroholding brokerage.
"But surely, foreign investors have been lured," he said.
Drugs concern Pliva and Zagrebacka Banka powered ahead, repeating Wednesday's excellent performance.
"Those two shares proved very attractive abroad. The stronger dollar has definitely also helped their cause... Furthermore, there is speculation about their half-year results," Nikolac said.
Pliva closed at an all-time high of 600 kuna, up 16 or 2.74 percent, but down from the intraday peak of 610 kuna. It was again the most actively traded issue with 9,516 shares sold.
Its Global Depository Receipts (GDRs) climbed to $18.325 from $17.6 at the open on the London Stock Exchange.

Zagrebacka's ordinaries rose 58 kuna to 2,582, also down from a record 2,585 earlier in the session. But only 235 shares changed hands. Its 1/10 GDRs fetched $39.125 -- highest price ever -- firming from Wednesday's $38.375.
Traders said selling offers for Zagrebacka were scarce.
The bank's preference stock added 100 kuna to 1,750 and its bearer shares were flat at 870 kuna on meagre volumes.
Thirteen of 18 issues traded on Thursday rose, only two fell and three closed flat. Volume shrank slightly to 24,782 units with turnover falling to 11.4 from 18.6 million kuna.
Fully-listed Varazdinska Banka's ordinaries led gainers, rising 26 kuna or 10.4 percent to 276 kuna on volume of 4,904.
Food processor Podravka firmed six kuna to 275, with 4,892 shares traded as its half-year results were also rumoured to have improved after losses in previous years, traders said.
Hotelier Arenaturist was the bigger of the two losers, falling one kuna to 105 with 148 shares traded. Jadranturist inched down one kuna to 261 on volume of 155.
Other tourist firms did better, with Laguna rising 47 kuna to 1,515 and Riviera climbing seven to end the day at 180 kuna. They sold 528 and 914 units, respectively.
